structured_output.summary:
Phase 18 delivers a genuinely good plan-and-inventory package. I verified the plan's technical claims against the actual SDK rather than its prose: `Mode::Response`/`Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults` exist and both widen enums (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:15-37, 717-732), `check_string` enforces exactly the ten kinds min/max/uuid/email/url/datetime/duration/date/rfc3339/regex (validation.rs:1143-1181), and the plan's bypass list is precisely the eight format kinds minus min/max — so policy item 1 is complete and unambiguous against the real implementation. `tools/g25_audit.py` produces a real deterministic ledger over all 47 vendor operations with full vendor and baseline field trees (requiredness, nullability, kind, checks), format sites, request UUID inventory and rejected query options; I spot-checked five operations against the vendor contract and Rust sources and found them accurate (target-profile error logs: only `limit`, skip/search rejected, `target_id` UUID-checked; `get_stream_detail` single `stream_id`; v1 `download_report` correctly paired to the opaque TS `z.unknown()` baseline while v2 `get_download_url` is correctly classified new). I independently confirmed all eleven "new" operations are genuinely absent from the frozen TypeScript baseline. The recorded checks in docs/checks/phase-18.json are real executions with exit codes and output, including an SDK-source freeze guard and an audit staleness guard, and docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json records both the Rust probe and the independent Zod run with raw stdout and an honest interpretation that refuses to claim the unavailable consumer loopback suite.

What blocks a 9 is evidence integrity on the phase's own headline requirement. Milestone 18 says "Retain direct reproduction and independent Zod outcomes", but the reproduction harness lives in `.local/g25-repro/`, which `.gitignore:3` excludes; the evidence file records SHA256 digests of files that are not in the repository, are not covered by `review_phase.fingerprint` (which only hashes tracked and non-ignored files), are not produced by any recorded phase-18 check command, and are not listed in the phase's scope_evidence. Nobody else can re-derive or re-run the single experiment the entire 0.2.2 policy rests on. Secondary gaps: the audit's provenance block names a file it never reads and omits the files it does read; the UUID inventory silently records an empty list if its method regex misses; the SDK-freeze check is weaker than the phase-15 precedent; the ledger does not quantify the blast radius of the global format bypass outside Red Team (I found ~60 `.uuid()/.datetime()/.email()/.url()` assertions in the frozen TypeScript source, including response schemas such as `AdapterResponseSchema`); and docs/implementation-plan.md was not given the follow-up section the Portkey track established as precedent.

findings.description: The direct reproduction and independent Zod harness is not retained in the repository. The recorded inputs (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/main.rs, cases.json, typescript.mts) resolve to .local/g25-repro/, which .gitignore:3 excludes from the repository; review_phase.fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:43-60) hashes only tracked and non-ignored files, and docs/checks/ is additionally excluded via EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES (tools/review_phase.py:13). No command in check_phase.commands_for(18) (tools/check_phase.py:71-76) produces or re-executes this evidence, and tools/test_g25.py does not assert its existence or content. Milestone 18 of the plan (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:83) requires retaining the direct reproduction and independent Zod outcomes; recording SHA256 digests of gitignored files is provenance that no third party, and no later phase, can verify or reproduce. The seven cases and both run transcripts are the sole factual basis for the claim that frozen Zod accepts strings the SDK rejects, i.e. for the whole 0.2.2 response policy.
findings.required_fix: Commit the reproduction harness inside the repository (for example contracts/compatibility/g25/repro/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs,cases.json,typescript.mts}, with .local paths resolved via the existing frozen TypeScript reference), add its execution to check_phase.commands_for(18) or to a recorded evidence generator so the outcomes are regenerable, list docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json and the harness in the phase 18 scope_evidence, and have tools/test_g25.py assert the committed cases match the recorded outcomes.

findings.description: The recorded input provenance is both wrong and incomplete. The paths list digests contracts/typescript.json, which audit() never reads, while omitting every other real input: contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json (line 31), contracts/native-operation-mappings/red-team*.json (line 34), contracts/manifest.json (line 61) and the Rust sources scanned for common::uuid calls (line 57). The vendor contract carries a per-operation sourceSha256 (for example contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json:3320) that the audit does not check before scanning the file, so the request-check half of the ledger is not source-bound.
findings.required_fix: Replace the hard-coded paths list with the actual inputs read during the run (vendor operations.json, the red-team mapping files, contracts/operations.json, contracts/manifest.json and schema_graph.json), drop contracts/typescript.json unless it is actually consumed, and verify each operation's recorded sourceSha256 against the scanned file before extracting UUID checks.

findings.description:
The request UUID inventory fails silently. If the `pub async fn <method>` regex does not match (for example a non-async or differently indented method), `match.group() if match else ''` yields an empty string and the operation is recorded with requestUuidArguments: [] — indistinguishable from an operation that genuinely performs no UUID check. Nine operations currently carry an empty list. Additionally `common::uuid\(([^)]+)\)` cannot capture nested parentheses, and the body boundary lookahead `(?=
    pub async fn |
}
|\Z)` silently over-captures into the next item if any non-`pub async fn` member separates two operations. The plan (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:63-67) requires this inventory to be complete because the retained checks must be enumerated in the changelog and compatibility report.
findings.required_fix: Raise instead of returning an empty body when the method cannot be located, make the body boundary tolerant of intervening members (or key extraction on nativeClass as well as nativeMethod), and handle nested parentheses in the argument capture; add a tools/test_g25.py assertion that the total extracted common::uuid count reconciles with the occurrences in the scanned Red Team sources.

findings.description: The phase-18 "no SDK implementation before plan acceptance" guard is weaker than the precedent it mirrors. `git diff --exit-code 7f4a062 -- crates/scm-sdk` ignores untracked files and covers only crates/scm-sdk, whereas the equivalent phase-15 guard (tools/test_portkey_access.py:126-132) checks Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/scm-sdk, LICENSE and NOTICE and additionally runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to catch untracked additions. Nothing currently violates the freeze, but the recorded evidence does not actually establish it.
findings.required_fix: Extend the phase-18 command list to cover Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE and NOTICE and to run `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` over those paths, matching the phase-15 precedent.

findings.description: Policy item 1 applies the string-format bypass "at the shared bounded validator so it covers every SDK response root", but the committed ledger covers only the 47 Red Team vendor operations. The frozen TypeScript source contains roughly 60 .uuid()/.datetime()/.email()/.url() assertions across 13 model files (.local/typescript/src/models/red-team.ts alone has 18), including response schemas such as AdapterResponseSchema (.local/typescript/src/models/red-team.ts:1266-1281), where the SDK will become strictly more permissive than the frozen baseline. The phase's own inventory therefore does not quantify the blast radius of the change it authorizes, and phase 19's "Cover non-Red-Team format validation too" has no enumerated target list to work from.
findings.required_fix: Extend tools/g25_audit.py (or add a companion section to contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json) to enumerate every non-Red-Team response root in schema_graph.json carrying a bypassed format check, and record in the plan that these are deliberate Rust differences from the frozen TypeScript baseline to be documented under AGENTS.md's export-parity clause.

findings.description: docs/implementation-plan.md has no section for the authorized G25 follow-up, although AGENTS.md:3 directs reading it when changing public contracts or acceptance criteria and this patch changes response-validation acceptance semantics. The Portkey follow-up set the precedent with the "Authorized Portkey access-policy addition" section at lines 160-164, and docs/implementation-plan.md was itself listed in phase 17 scope_evidence.
findings.required_fix: Add a short "G25 response compatibility patch" section to docs/implementation-plan.md linking docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md, stating the 0.2.2 target, the response-mode format relaxation and the retained request strictness.

findings.description: Phase 18 scope_evidence lists only three files and omits artifacts that are part of this phase's deliverable and were changed or created for it: tools/test_g25.py, tools/check_phase.py, docs/PHASES.md and docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json. Phase 17 (lines 3469-3522) enumerates every such artifact, so the reviewer prompt generated from this entry under-describes the change.
findings.required_fix: Add tools/test_g25.py, tools/check_phase.py, docs/PHASES.md, docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json and the committed reproduction harness to the phase 18 scope_evidence list.

findings.description: Maintainability defects in the audit tool: the PREFIX constant is never used; the synthetic array-wrapper row inserted at line 50 omits the 'node' key that every other row carries, so consumers cannot assume a uniform record shape; ZodCatch is flattened at line 12 alongside Optional/Default/Nullable, discarding the fact that a catch silently substitutes a value (material when the baseline is used as a compatibility floor); and the CSV operation is represented only as responseRoot: null (contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json:38243) rather than carrying the vendor's explicit responseHandling: "csv_bytes" label that the plan at line 15-16 claims is an explicit classification.
